response: The Greek Dark Ages, also known as the Homeric Age, are the years following the fall of the Mycenaean civilization, roughly from 1100 to 700 BC. This period is characterized by a lack of historical records and a decline in material culture, but it is also the time when Homer composed the Iliad and the Odyssey, which provide insight into the social and cultural life of the period. The Dark Ages saw the gradual rise of the Greek city-states, which would later become the cradle of Western civilization.
